owner: KDE native-document observation adapter; existing result verifier and context reducer retain authority
first_failed_transition: Chrome can report the exact selection created by a successful native edit before CommitText becomes visible. native_observation_failed(native_selection_present) discards the current native binding and revokes word state. When the actual replacement arrives, the unchanged common verifier censors the result because that binding was destroyed. R18 active-burst gesture4 demonstrates this order. The later bd2a751e fixed20 run removes selection deadlines but still records selection_present, censored native results and closed-word/source-state failures.
decision: Treat selection_present as an in-flight observation only while an exact native result is already pending for the current token, epoch, focus, lease, layout and identical field. Reuse the existing transient-read path: remove all current document-derived edit proof and await a fresh complete unselected observation. Keep the original pending result and its existing expiry/verifier. Selection alone never confirms an edit, creates an owner, extends a result deadline or grants another mutation. All ordinary selection loss without this pending exact result still revokes.
verification: Positive source control: intermediate selection clears snapshot/edit route, retains the current pending result, then a complete actual final snapshot settles through the unchanged verifier and admission publication.

Negative source controls: absent pending/native/exact result; changed epoch, focus, lease, layout, field, privacy, sealed handoff and GNOME never retain the native subscription through selection loss.

Retain the independent selection-acknowledgement trial. Repeat unchanged r18 fixed20 and first/second-word Chrome presentation after byte-verified KDE installation. No full Chrome acceptance inferred from a subset.
